analysis.title: Biggest "Surprise" In 19 Years: Goldman's Garrett Sees Echoes Of COVID, GFC, & Liberation Day As Panic Index Explodes
key_insights: On Thursday the Nasdaq 100 fell 6.4%, its worst day since March 2020, and the S&P fell 4.4%, its worst since Liberation Day. Traders bought more puts than on any day in Cboe history.

Garrett's verdict is that the move 'still feels more like violent positioning reset than systemic event.' He says exposures are 'materially lower' and protection 'was finally chased at the index level.' He also says there is 'clearly more mechanical supply to work through.'
Thursday was far less stressful than 2020 (VIX 70+), 2009 (VIX 60+) and 2025 (VIX 50+), according to Garrett, who was in the seat for all three.
About $2.5 trillion of Nasdaq 100 market cap was lost in one session, the largest one-day dollar loss in Goldman's dataset since 2001.

Thursday's dollar notional traded was 'the largest regular session volume ever' excluding opex and index rebalance days. The article reads about $1.75 trillion off Garrett's chart, above the April 2025 tariff panic.

Thursday was the third-largest dollar notional ETF day in history. ETFs were 33% of the consolidated tape versus a 28% average. Garrett attributes this to VVIX rallying 40+ points in a day, which pushes investors to ETFs first.
Clients had 'aggressively taken off protection following Wednesday's post midterm election rally.' That left investors underhedged going into Thursday's volatility.

VVIX jumped about 44 points, the second-largest one-day move since 2006, behind only the February 2018 Volmageddon spike. On a delta-adjusted basis, 1-month VIX outperformance was among the biggest of the past five years, comparable to Aug 5, 2024 and Liberation Day.

SPX 3-month implied correlation rose about 9 points in one session to just over 20, one of the largest one-day jumps since 2023. Last week 12-month implied correlation was about 20%, so 2027 was priced as one of the most dispersive years ever.

Garrett's 'move surprise ratio' (MSR) divides an asset's 1-day percentage change by its prior-day 1-month implied vol. Thursday's S&P MSR was the largest since at least 2007, above the GFC, Volmageddon and Covid. QQQ posted its second-largest MSR, behind Liberation Day, and the Russell 2000 posted a top-five reading.

Garrett's panic index is an equal-weighted percentile rank of VIX, SPX skew, SPX term structure and SPX 1-month ATM implied vol. It hit 9.57 on Thursday and closed the week at 9.2. Garrett says readings above 9 have historically been a good buying opportunity, though the 9+ cluster around Liberation Day lasted a few weeks before the bottom.

Dip-buyers are favouring 'vol lower' trades. On Friday investors bought VIX puts rather than SPX or NDX calls, and the VIX put/call volume ratio reached about 1.5, the highest on Garrett's two-year chart.

Goldman's Prime book was net sold, 'driven almost entirely by long selling.' US fundamental L/S gross leverage fell 8.7 points to 207.5% (26th percentile, 1 year) and net fell 3.7 points to 43.4% (1st percentile). Beta-adjusted gross is 213.2% (-15.7) and net is 57.5% (-6.4), both in the 0th percentile.
Single names were net sold for the 8th consecutive week, with the largest supply in more than four months. The rotation was out of tech and industrials and into utilities, real estate and financials.

Global tech selling matched the largest in Goldman's dataset, and four of the five biggest tech net-selling weeks on record came in the past five months. TMT long/short funds are roughly flat on the year, down from +24% in June.

Goldman's high-beta momentum pair is in a 50% drawdown, deeper than the 2021 unwind and the deepest since the series began in 2011. Realized vol across 20 flagship custom baskets hit 93 on a one-week basis, the highest since Liberation Day.
The six-month return spread between 'broad AI' and the S&P ex-AI is -37%, the lowest in the ten-year chart. It was nearly +70% just over a year ago.

Goldman's high-touch desk was a net seller of $6B on the week, mostly tech, and has sold $30B of tech (TMT plus comm services) since the decline began, more than the $21B of supply in July. Friday's close brought the first buy skew in semiconductors in 6+ sessions.
CTA signals are negative in about 60% of global equity markets. Goldman calculates $28B of S&P futures to sell over the next week and $45B over the next month.

In bonds, CTAs have bought $33M DV01 and are modeled to buy another $28M next week and $78M next month. The article notes this comes as payrolls printed 165K and the market prices a December Fed hike.

Goldman's Delta One desk likes shorting its diversified staples basket (GSXUSTAP). Staples trade at about 22.5x the 24-month forward multiple versus about 10.5x for the semiconductor index. The desk says that with rates where they are, 'you get paid to be short on swap.'
Garrett expects 'more technical wood to chop in the short run.' He would buy December upside call spreads across the most washed-out indices and sectors (long delta, flat vol, fade call skew).

Garrett frames the open question as 'whether this represents another painful positioning reset or the beginning of something more consequential.' Goldman's Delta One head is betting on 1998, not 2000. Tony Pasquariello sees one last push higher before a tougher 2027. BofA's Michael Hartnett says the blue wave marked 'peak AI.'

market_movers.rationale: Goldman's Delta One desk likes shorting its diversified staples basket. Staples trade at about 22.5x forward multiple versus about 10.5x for semiconductors, and the desk says the short pays on swap.

sector_views.rationale: Record tech net selling and a 50% high-beta momentum drawdown, but Garrett would buy December call spreads in washed-out names such as SOXX, SMH and XLK. Semis saw their first buy skew in 6+ sessions on Friday.
Staples trade at about 22.5x the 24-month forward multiple versus about 10.5x for semiconductors. Goldman's Delta One desk likes shorting the staples basket, saying 'safe is expensive.'
Prime book data shows funds buying these sectors in a defensive rotation while selling tech and industrials. The article does not state a Goldman view on them.

macro_indicators.interpretation: The article says payrolls 'blew out' to 165K and the market prices a December Fed hike, which sits against the CTA buying of duration.
The article says the Fed may hike into the deleveraging, and that unlike 1998 there is no Greenspan cut coming.

tension_points.bull_case: Garrett says it 'still feels more like violent positioning reset than systemic event.' Exposures are materially lower, protection was chased at the index level, nets are at the 0th percentile, and panic index readings above 9 have historically been good buying opportunities.
tension_points.bear_case: There is 'clearly more mechanical supply to work through' ($28B of S&P futures to sell next week via CTAs). The Fed may hike into the deleveraging, and the AI financing question is unanswered. BofA's Hartnett says the blue wave marked 'peak AI.'
tension_points.what_invalidates: A repeat of the Liberation Day pattern, where the cluster of panic index readings above 9 lasted a few weeks before the bottom, or continued CTA selling and a December Fed hike.
